description: Blocks DISPATCHING a new subagent (the Agent/Task tool, opencode's `task` tool, or omp's `task` tool) while the machine's real memory pressure is at WARN-or-worse (macOS `sysctl kern.memorystatus_vm_pressure_level` >= RIG_FLEET_DISPATCH_BLOCK_AT_LEVEL, default 2; 1=normal/2=warn/4=critical — the same signal Activity Monitor's Memory Pressure graph and the OS's own OOM killer read, not a noisy raw free-byte count). Closes the still-open 'pre-agent gate for Agent/Task dispatch (fan-out itself)' scope note from agent-tools#579, after both the 2026-08-27/28 incident (~10-15 concurrent background agents drove free memory to ~65MB on a 24GB machine, hanging several VS Code windows) and the 2026-09-08 JetsamEvent mass-kill (13 omp + 46 node + 20 Python processes concurrently, swap at 86%, 35+ low-priority daemons killed first). Deliberately stateless — no counter, no lock file, no queue — every invocation re-reads real pressure fresh, so nothing can leak a slot or deadlock a second hook (a subagent dying mid-run, which is routine, would otherwise leak a counted slot forever); a retry after genuine memory frees up passes. No self-bypass and deliberately no Telegram hatch-escalation (this is an objective, self-resolving fact, not a human judgment call). Unlike `background-subagent-gate` (the sibling pre-agent hook, which exempts dispatches made from inside a subagent via `agent_id`), this hook applies identically to the orchestrator's own dispatch AND a subagent's further fan-out — the risk (one more agent process on an already-strained machine) does not depend on which layer of the fan-out tree issues the call. Fails open (allows) when no reliable pressure signal is available (non-macOS without PSI, or the sysctl call itself fails) — this is an availability circuit-breaker, not a security boundary. on_error=open. Sibling: `heavy-op-memory-gate` gates the same real signal at the pre-bash level (a heavy build/test/review command actually starting); this hook gates the fan-out act itself — together they cover both halves of the memory-safety story.
